mechanisms.label: Diesel / refining crisis
mechanisms.summary: The available evidence indicates that refinery availability constraints are tightening diesel and jet fuel supplies, independent of crude price movements. A drone strike on the Kstovo refinery in Russia is expected to reduce output of key units (CDU, hydrocracker, catalytic cracker), leading to a short‑term tightening in diesel/product balances and a geopolitical risk premium on Russian downstream assets. Bloomberg reports a global diesel crunch that will keep prices high and dampen demand, suggesting a refining bottleneck. Argus media notes increased VGO exports and reduced imports due to refinery maintenance, further supporting a supply constraint. No official sources directly link Brent prices to these events, but the evidence collectively points to a refining‑driven scarcity rather than a crude shortage.
